clue.text: Exceptionally large jeans manufactured outside a place in 25

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside the size abbreviation, wrapping round it
manufactured means made up, so the letters of jeans are made into a new order

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Oversized denim being produced in a Californian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptionally large' is the clothing label for outsize; 'manufactured' is the anagram signal and 'outside' the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: San Jose is a large city in Silicon Valley, part of the state given at 25.

clue.text: A city in 25 said to have gone and changed

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the two words are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A Californian city is rumoured to have disappeared and been transformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges the letters of SAID and GONE together; 'to have' and 'and' just link.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is the big port city in the far south of the state given at 25.

clue.text: Something juicy in a centre spread

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tasty filling spread across the middle of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a foodstuff in the surface but is the anagram signal for IN A CENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned peach variety, a fruit full of juice.

clue.text: Some booze killed a sumo wrestler

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Drink proved fatal to a big Japanese wrestler.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozeki is the second-highest rank in professional sumo, just below yokozuna.

clue.text: Noun in English loosely meaning 'train driver'

indicators.note: in places the two abbreviations inside the rearranged word
loosely suggests something not held in its usual form, so the letters of meaning are jumbled

parts.note: N is the grammar abbreviation for noun

explanation.surface: A dictionary note: an English noun whose loose sense is a locomotive driver.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a dictionary entry; 'loosely' is the anagram signal and 'in' the insertion, giving a hyphenated word.
explanation.definitionFit: An old term for the person who works a locomotive, the driver of a railway engine.

clue.text: Fine real estate borders a port in 25

indicators.note: borders means lies on either side of, so the two letters for fine go round the a

parts.note: OK means fine, all right
real estate is property in the form of land

explanation.surface: Smart property surrounds a harbour city in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' is not a quality of the estate here but the word for all right; 'borders' means the two letters sit either side of the a.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakland is a port city on the east side of San Francisco Bay in the state at 25.

clue.text: He had a successful running career, mostly completed not having any shorts!

definitions.text: He had a successful running career

indicators.note: mostly tells us to drop the last letter of the word for completed

parts.note: completed means finished, over
shorts are small drinks of spirits, so someone who has none is TT, teetotal

explanation.surface: A runner's career ended without him ever wearing running shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of OVER, leaving OVE. Steve Ovett was a British middle-distance runner, 1980 Olympic 800m champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve Ovett was an Olympic champion athlete, so his career was spent running, and successfully.

clue.text: Ace dealt up after king — it could win you money

indicators.note: after places the reversed word behind the king's letter

parts.note: K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom, so the word for ace is turned round

parts.note: an ace counts as one

explanation.surface: A card game: an ace turned over after a king pays out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'dealt up' reverses the word; 'after' sets it behind the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Keno is a lottery-style gambling game in which a player may win a cash prize.

clue.text: A Spaniard's welcome to return to Australia, and welcome in part of America

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so the Spanish greeting is read backwards

parts.note: hola is Spanish for hello

explanation.surface: A Spanish greeting comes back to Australia, a greeting in another region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses the Spanish hello; the part of America is Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawaii is a US state, and its traditional greeting is used for both hello and goodbye.

clue.text: Magician's act entertaining a lot of people in turn

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: act means do, perform

indicators.note: in turn means turned round, so the word for a lot of people is reversed

parts.note: a lot of people are many

explanation.surface: A conjuror's show amuses a big crowd one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' reverses MANY to YNAM, which DO is 'entertaining'. Dynamo is the stage name of British TV magician Steven Frayne.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage name of a well-known British illusionist, star of the TV series Magician Impossible.

clue.text: Mini cheese sandwiches for a particular market

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the letters lie inside the words given

explanation.surface: Small cheese rolls aimed at a specialist group of customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food but hides the letters across MINI CHEESE.
explanation.definitionFit: In business, a specialised segment of customers with distinct needs is called by this word.

clue.text: An inexperienced kid not fully prepared to play an instrument

parts.note: green means unripe, not ready
a horn is a brass musical instrument

explanation.surface: A novice child who isn't quite ready to perform on an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer or novice lacking experience, a raw beginner.

clue.text: European-looking climbing plant found in international gallery

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the plant sits within the gallery

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
a liana is a woody climbing vine of tropical forests

explanation.surface: A climbing plant with a continental look is spotted in an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is London's best-known art gallery, so 'gallery' in crosswords often means it; 'found in' puts the plant inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Means in the style of Italy, which is a European country, so looking like something from there.

clue.text: Resort in 25 is well surrounded by trees

indicators.note: surrounded by means encircled, so the word for well goes inside the word for trees

parts.note: palms are tropical trees
a well is a source of water, as is a spring

explanation.surface: A Californian resort has a water source ringed by trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' puts the water source inside the trees, splitting the plural before its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm Springs is a desert resort city in Southern California, the state at 25.

clue.text: Training with the French football legend

parts.note: PE is physical education, school training
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French sports coach working with a famous footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brazilian forward, three-time World Cup winner, is among the greatest players of the game.

clue.text: Sound blokes making an appearance

indicators.note: Sound tells us the word for blokes is heard, not spelt

parts.note: blokes are men, guys

explanation.surface: Decent men turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable but signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: An outward form or semblance, how something presents itself.

clue.text: What kippers do mostly around other fish

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the shortened word reads backwards
mostly drops the final letter

parts.note: to kip is to sleep, so kippers are sleepers here

explanation.surface: Smoked herrings swimming among different fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kippers' looks like smoked fish but means people who kip, so they sleep. 'mostly' cuts SLEEP to SLEE and 'around' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Long snake-like fish, different from the herring kind suggested by kippers.

clue.text: Yet more rioting besieges Northern bay in 25

indicators.note: besieges means surrounds, so the jumble encloses the letter
rioting means running wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Further unrest encircles a northern bay in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' rearranges YET MORE, and that 'besieges' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Monterey Bay is a large inlet on the central coast of the state at 25.

clue.text: Being smart, I sheltered in the last bit of rain with a dry head

indicators.note: sheltered in means kept inside, so the letter I goes within the other pieces
the last bit of picks the final letter of rain

parts.note: dry means teetotal, TT
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Looking smart, I took cover from the end of the rain, keeping my head dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland, not a body part; 'sheltered in' puts I inside the string near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neat and smart, so this noun is the quality of being smartly dressed.

clue.text: A bit on the side giving former partner stress

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
stress is strain, tension

explanation.surface: An affair causes an ex-partner anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit on the side' suggests a lover but means an added part, as on a building.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe or addition built onto the side of a house.

clue.text: Dried fish may be storable

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form something else, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: Preserved fish can be kept for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Herrings cured by salting and light smoking, a kind of preserved fish.

clue.text: Source material is impressively put together

parts.note: a well is a source of water
knit is knitted fabric

explanation.surface: The original fabric has been assembled impressively.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes something soundly constructed or a body that is sturdy and compact.

clue.text: Applaud when old road tax gets cut

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: gets cut means shortened, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a toll is a charge for using a road

explanation.surface: Cheering when a former road charge is reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets cut' trims TOLL to TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise enthusiastically, to laud or celebrate.

clue.text: Great — and mostly safe — region of 25

parts.note: great means big

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter

parts.note: safe means certain, sure

explanation.surface: A splendid and largely secure part of California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SURE to SUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Big Sur is a rugged stretch of Pacific coastline in the state at 25.

clue.text: One satisfied when returning an article of clothing, for example

definitions.text: an article of clothing, for example

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: met means satisfied, as a demand is met

explanation.surface: A shopper, happy with a garment, brings it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses the word for satisfied, as in a need being fulfilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment is one example of a single object in a list or collection.

clue.text: Lie about taking cocaine, creating an ostentatious display

indicators.note: taking means swallowing up, so one piece holds another
about means turned round, so the word for lie is reversed

parts.note: a tale is a lie, a fib
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: Lying about drug use makes a showy spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses TALE to ELAT, which is 'taking' C.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant show or conspicuous success, dazzling effect.

clue.text: Fail to distribute crop outside Iowa and another state

indicators.note: outside places the cereal word around the jumbled letters

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

indicators.note: to distribute means to spread around, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: IA is the postal abbreviation for the state of Iowa

explanation.surface: A farming failure in Iowa and a neighbouring state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to distribute' rearranges the first word; 'outside' wraps the cereal round it, and Iowa's postal code follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state, so it is another one beside Iowa mentioned in the clue.

clue.text: Wow, you can see this at Hampton Court?

definitions.meaning: to wow is to astonish or stun

definitions.text: you can see this at Hampton Court?
definitions.meaning: Hampton Court Palace near London has a famous hedge labyrinth; split, the letters read as one such puzzle

explanation.surface: Visitors are dazzled by a famous sight at a royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into an article plus noun. Hampton Court is a Tudor palace by the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone greatly, to bowl them over.

clue.text: Peripheral networking device doesn't start

indicators.note: doesn't start means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a router is a box that links computer networks

explanation.surface: An add-on piece of network kit won't boot up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peripheral' looks like computer hardware, matching the surface, but is an adjective meaning on the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: On the edge or fringe, far from the centre.

clue.text: Down American wine here in 25?

parts.note: down is soft fluff, like the nap on fabric

explanation.surface: An invitation to drink American wine from California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like a verb meaning drink, but is soft fibre, NAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Napa Valley is California's best-known wine-growing region.

clue.text: Being mindful of your actions feels unusual when accepting a fight

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the jumble holds the other pieces
unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: war is a fight

explanation.surface: Being conscious of one's behaviour feels strange when taking on a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' gives SELFE, which is 'accepting' the battle with its article just before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Having conscious knowledge of one's own character and conduct.

clue.text: Combined effect of acid and ecstasy is rubbish

parts.note: acid is LSD, whose effect is a trip
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Mixing two drugs is a bad idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense, worthless talk or writing; literally, cow's stomach eaten as food.

clue.text: The daily struggle of people pursuing a renegade

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so the word for people comes after

parts.note: a rat is a deserter or traitor
a race is a people

explanation.surface: A daily grind for those chasing a defector.
explanation.definitionFit: The competitive routine of working life, the endless scramble.
